title: The King They Crucified
paragraphs: As soon as the sun was up, the religious leaders put the final touches on their shady plan to execute Jesus. They tied him up and hauled him off to the governor, Pilate, like a criminal.

When Judas, the friend who betrayed him, realized Jesus was actually going to be killed, he totally lost it. Overcome with guilt, he tried to give the thirty silver coins back to the high priests. 'I sinned! I betrayed an innocent man!' he cried. They shot back, 'What do we care? That's your problem.' Judas threw the money into the Temple, ran out, and hung himself. The high priests picked up the silver pieces but didn't know what to do with them — 'We can't put this blood money, a payment for murder, into the Temple offering.' So they used it to buy the 'Potter's Field' as a burial ground for the homeless. That's how it got the name 'Murder Meadow,' and the name stuck to this day. And just like that, Jeremiah's words came true: they took the thirty silver pieces — the price set on him by the people of Israel — and bought the potter's field, following God's instructions to the letter without even realizing it.

Jesus stood before Governor Pilate, who asked him, 'Are you the King of the Jews?' Jesus replied with a quiet confidence, 'You said it.' But when the priests and elders started piling on the accusations, Jesus didn't say a word. Pilate was baffled. 'Don't you hear all this stuff they're accusing you of?' he asked. Still, Jesus remained silent. The governor was seriously impressed.

It was a custom to release one prisoner chosen by the crowd during the Passover festival. They had a famous bad guy named Barabbas in jail. Pilate, knowing the religious leaders were just jealous, asked the crowd, 'Who should I release? Barabbas, or Jesus, the so-called Christ?' Right in the middle of this, while court was still in session, Pilate's wife sent him a message: 'Don't get mixed up in judging this noble man. I just went through a long, troubled night because of a dream about him.' But the high priests and religious leaders had already talked the crowd into demanding the pardon of Barabbas and the execution of Jesus. 'What should I do with Jesus, the so-called Christ?' Pilate asked. They all shouted, 'Nail him to a cross!' Pilate pushed back, 'But for what crime?' But they just yelled all the louder, 'Nail him to a cross!'

Pilate saw a riot was about to pop off and that he was getting nowhere. He washed his hands in front of everyone and dropped a bomb: 'I'm innocent of this man's blood. This is on you.' The crowd went nuts, shouting, 'We'll take the blame! Us and our kids!' So Pilate freed Barabbas, had Jesus brutally whipped, and handed him over to be crucified.

The governor's soldiers took Jesus into the palace and the whole squad gathered to make fun of him. They stripped him and put a scarlet robe on him, twisted a crown of thorns for his head, and put a staff in his hand like a fake scepter. They knelt down, mocking him, 'Hey, hail King of the Jews!' Then they spit on him and beat him on the head with the staff. When they were done, they put his own clothes back on and led him away to be killed.

On the way out, they forced a random guy from Cyrene, Simon, to carry Jesus' heavy cross. They got to Golgotha, which means 'Skull Hill.' They offered Jesus wine mixed with a painkiller, but after tasting it, he refused. They nailed him to the cross, and then gambled for his clothes. Above his head, they posted the charge: THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS. They crucified two criminals with him, one on his right and one on his left.

People walking by hurled insults, shaking their heads. 'You were gonna destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, right? So save yourself! If you're the Son of God, get down from that cross!' The religious leaders joined in the trash talk: 'He saved others, but he can't save himself! King of Israel, huh? Let's see him come down from the cross, and then we'll believe! He trusted God? Let God rescue him now if he wants him!' Even the criminals crucified next to him dissed him.

From noon until three in the afternoon, the whole land went dark. Around three, Jesus cried out in agony, 'Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?' which means, 'My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?' Some of the bystanders who heard him said, 'He's calling for Elijah.' One of them ran and soaked a sponge in sour wine, lifted it up on a stick so he could drink. The others joked, 'Don't be in such a hurry — let's see if Elijah comes and saves him.' Then Jesus cried out loudly one more time and breathed his last. At that moment, the massive Temple curtain ripped in two from top to bottom. The earth shook, rocks split, and tombs opened. What's more, many bodies of believers asleep in their graves were raised — after Jesus' resurrection, they left the tombs, entered the holy city, and appeared to many people. The Roman captain and his soldiers who were guarding Jesus were terrified by the earthquake and everything happening. They said, 'Seriously, this man was the Son of God.'

Quite a few women were watching from a distance — women who had followed Jesus all the way from Galilee to take care of Him. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of James and John.

That evening, a rich guy named Joseph from Arimathea showed up. He was a follower of Jesus too. He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus' body, and Pilate gave the green light. Joseph took the body, wrapped it in fresh, clean linen, and laid it in his own brand-new tomb that had been carved out of rock. Then he rolled a massive stone in front of the entrance and left. Mary Magdalene and the other Mary just sat there across from the tomb, watching.

The next day (the day after Preparation Day), the chief priests and Pharisees went to Pilate. 'Sir,' they said, 'we remember that liar said while he was still alive, ‘After three days I will rise again.’ So order the tomb to be locked down tight until day three. Otherwise his disciples might sneak in, steal the body, and tell everyone he rose from the dead. That last lie would be even worse than the first.' Pilate said, 'Take some guards. Go secure it the best you know how.' So they went, sealed the stone, and posted the guards.
